content.thinking:
I'm putting together the JSON spec now, with the outcomes in the order reject, escalate, return, incomplete, approve, and the order SOP set to 2.1. For the unknowns case I'm using the wording from SOP 2.2, that a claim can't be approved while any required fact is unknown, and I'm marking it incomplete. Next I'm starting on the rules, beginning with 3.1 on rejecting when days to submission run too long.

I'm working through the rules in order now, setting the day cutoff at 61 days, rejecting self-approved claims, and escalating totals of $5,000 or more without director sign-off. I'm also adding the receipt requirement for lines of $75 or more, the alcohol return rule, and the gift and business-class escalations.

I'm working through the rest of the rules, checking how the airfare exception for pre-approved business-class fares sits against the escalation rule. Since escalate ranks above approve, that exception wouldn't change the outcome, and I'm weighing whether an approve rule is needed at all, given that the procedure never says what happens when nothing else applies.

I'm weighing whether a default approve rule belongs in the spec, since the procedure never states what happens when no other outcome applies and only says that approval is blocked while a required fact is unknown. I'm leaning toward a section 1 rule with an empty condition, citing the outcome definition that approve means paying the claim.

I'm settling on an approve default with an empty condition, since approve is the lowest outcome and only applies when nothing else does. The 4.5 pre-approved business-class exception I'm writing as stated, even though escalate outranks it and it will never change the result.

I'm now settling the remaining fact-handling: the claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense, and I'm noting that as the unknown-when-empty text. The 4.5 pre-approved exception stays as written, and I'm leaving out lines under $75 because the receipt rule doesn't reach them.

Mapping the cabin and category words from the SOP to the values the spec will use: business and first class under cabin, and alcohol, gift and airfare under category.

I'm checking whether any needs are missing from the facts: days_to_submit, total_usd and recipient_official are all given, so the needs list stays empty. I'm also treating the director sign-off as a plain no-or-yes fact, with the escalate rule applying only when it isn't signed.

I'm deciding whether to include headings for sections 2, 3 and 4 as well as the real subsections, and I'm leaning toward listing only the numbered rules and notes so nothing extra gets added.

I'm settling on the wording for the default approve rule, which only needs to say pay the claim, and I'm weighing whether the sentence should carry the "Approve:" label or just the words after it.

I'm settling on the exact wording for the approve default, using the words "pay the claim." and checking the case, since the source has it in lowercase. I'm also weighing whether a default approve rule might collide with the unknowns handling, but since it always applies, it never leaves a fact-dependent outcome in question.

I'm writing out the business-class and first-class airfare rule, which says to escalate any claim with such a line.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.unknown_when_empty: which lines (receipts or expenses) the claim has
lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes and says a claim is a list of lines. Approve ('pay the claim') is the outcome when no more severe rule applies; this follows from 2.1 placing Approve last. Section 1 is also the source for the lines collection.
Sets the order of outcomes, most severe first: reject, escalate, return, incomplete, approve (order / order_sop).
Says an unknown fact is not false and blocks approval. This sets the unknowns outcome to incomplete.

Translated as written. 4.4 escalates every business-class airfare line, and under 2.1 Escalate outranks Approve, so this approve rule can never decide a claim. The SOP does not say that 4.5 is an exception to 4.4. A person should decide how 4.4 and 4.5 relate.
